question_stem: A novelist ends a chapter at the moment a character discovers an unexpected message, leaving its contents undisclosed until the next chapter. This technique is best described as:
answer_explanation: A cliffhanger ends a section of a narrative at a suspenseful or unresolved moment, encouraging the reader to continue to discover what happens next. A denouement brings the main conflicts towards resolution; exposition supplies background information; a flashback presents an earlier event.

question_stem: A character tells a younger sibling, “A stitch in time saves nine,” after the sibling ignores a small repair. The character uses the saying mainly to:
option_A: draw on traditional wisdom to advise that prompt action can prevent a bigger problem
option_B: give performers instructions about movement and position on stage
option_C: reveal private thoughts in a speech that other characters cannot hear
option_D: establish a pattern of repeated sounds at the ends of poetic lines
answer_explanation: “A stitch in time saves nine” is a proverb. It expresses the practical wisdom that dealing with a small problem promptly may prevent it from becoming a larger one. In dialogue, a proverb can communicate shared cultural knowledge or advice concisely.

question_stem: A speaker says that an elderly person has “passed away” instead of saying that the person has died. This expression is an example of:
answer_explanation: A euphemism is a mild or indirect expression used in place of one that may be considered harsh, unpleasant or offensive. “Passed away” is a common indirect expression for “died”.

question_stem: A traditional Shakespearean sonnet follows which rhyme scheme?
answer_explanation: A Shakespearean sonnet is conventionally arranged in three quatrains followed by a rhyming couplet, giving the rhyme scheme ABAB CDCD EFEF GG.
